change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses stripe-node 17.3.0 pinned to 2024-09-30.acacia, so nothing breaks today; the endive changes only apply once the repo moves. Bringing the SDK current (23.x) forces the API version to endive in one coherent PR. That PR must:
- update apiVersion at lib/actions.ts:13;
- remove payment_method_types from the Checkout Session create (otherwise a 400 on every checkout, a highly visible break of the subscription purchase flow);
- confirm the client uses `new Stripe()` (v22);
- confirm webhook constructEvent usage (v21);
- re-check subscription response fields affected by the basil-era moves (current_period_* to items).

Uncertain: the response handling was not scanned, so the migration agent should read how subscriptions.retrieve/list results and webhook event objects are consumed. Urgency is medium because there is no forced cutoff (the pinned version keeps working), but the payment_method_types break is severe when the upgrade happens.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23.0.0 pins 2026-09-30.endive. In TypeScript the apiVersion literal in lib/actions.ts:13 must match the SDK, so the SDK bump and the move from 2024-09-30.acacia to endive are one edit.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. Only bites once the repo is on endive. checkout.sessions.create at lib/actions.ts:135 passes payment_method_types, which must be removed in the same PR (rely on dynamic payment methods / Dashboard settings) or Stripe returns a 400.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. An intermediate API major crossed when jumping from acacia to endive. Its breaking items (ui_mode enum values, events_from, Capabilities risk requirements) are not used by the repo's calls, so no separate move is needed.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. An intermediate stripe-node major skipped over by going 17.3.0 -> 23. The migration agent must make sure the client is built with `new Stripe(...)` and adapt to the reworked types.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:node-21-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 21.0.0: pins 2026-03-25.dahlia, drops Node 16, decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal, wrong webhook parsing method throws, effective 2026-03-25. An intermediate stripe-node major. It pins dahlia, Stripe.Decimal types and stricter webhook parsing (the wrong parsing method now throws). The constructEvent call in app/api/webhook/route.ts:13 should be verified as part of the same upgrade.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "All `decimal_string` fields changed type from `string` to `Stripe.Decimal` in both request params and response objects."
- stripe:node-20-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 20.0.0: pins 2025-11-17.clover; v2 array params use indexed serialization (may break mock-server tests), effective 2025-11-18. An intermediate stripe-node major (clover pin, v2 array serialization). The repo uses no v2 endpoints, so it is covered by the single bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break any unit tests that expect the latter behavior when setting up a mock server."
- stripe:node-19-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 19.0.0: pins 2025-09-30.clover; parseThinEvent renamed parseEventNotification, v2 delete returns V2DeletedObject, v2 nullable props optional; 19.x deprecated (Files API timeout bug), effective 2025-09-30. An intermediate stripe-node major (parseThinEvent rename, v2 delete shape). The repo uses neither, so it is covered by the single bump.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Rename function `StripeClient.parseThinEvent` to `StripeClient.parseEventNotification` and remove the `Stripe.ThinEvent` interface."

callSites.why: The Stripe client pins apiVersion '2024-09-30.acacia'. Upgrading stripe-node to 23 requires changing this to '2026-09-30.endive' (the TS types enforce the pinned version).
checkout.sessions.create passes payment_method_types, which is removed on endive and returns 400 payment_method_types_no_longer_supported. Delete the param.

webhooks.constructEvent: verify signature parsing still works under the v21+ stricter parsing (raw body, correct method). The event payload shapes change with the new API version, so the handler's field reads should be checked.

subscriptions.retrieve: jumping from acacia crosses 2025-03-31.basil, which moved current_period_start/current_period_end from Subscription to subscription items. Check which response fields are read (the response handling was not scanned).
subscriptions.list: the request params are unchanged, but the response typing/shape changed across basil and the v22 type rework. Verify the fields read from the results.

record.prBody:
## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Upgraded stripe 17.3.0 to 23.0.0 with npm. Set apiVersion to 2026-09-30.endive in lib/actions.ts and app/api/webhook/route.ts. Removed payment_method_types from checkout.sessions.create. Added scripts/check-stripe-migration.js. The repo already used `new Stripe()`, constructEvent, and no current_period_* reads, so nothing else changed. Typecheck and build pass.

Files touched:
- `app/api/webhook/route.ts`
- `lib/actions.ts`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-stripe-migration.js`

### Why

stripe-node 23 types only accept the endive apiVersion, and endive removes payment_method_types from Checkout Sessions, which would return a 400 on every checkout.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| stripe-migration | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- stripe-migration, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db' STRIPE_SECRET_KEY='sk_test_placeholder' STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET='whsec_placeholder' AUTH_SECRET='placeholder' GEMINI_API_KEY='placeholder'; node scripts/check-stripe-migration.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `stripe__stripe_check_params`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- stripe__stripe_check_params: pass (POST /v1/checkout/sessions at 2026-09-30.endive: no problems)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (@prisma/client's postinstall was skipped, so the Prisma client types are not generated. Typecheck and build import PrismaClient and models from it.); it exited 0.
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (Postinstall scripts were off, so the Prisma client (@prisma/client) was never generated; typecheck and build import its types and models.); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, AUTH_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY.

Test of this change: `stripe-migration`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Endive response shapes (subscriptions.list/retrieve status, checkout.session.completed fields) not verified live
- Webhook handler and subscription code were not exercised against real events

### Behaviour changes

- Checkout no longer restricts to card; the payment methods shown now follow Dashboard settings (dynamic payment methods)
- Requires Node >=20 at deploy
- The dashboard webhook endpoint API version should be aligned to endive

preparation.reasoning:
The schema uses prisma-client-js and the repo has no postinstall script, so the client must be generated explicitly. prisma generate needs DATABASE_URL to be set only to load the schema, and it does not connect to a database. The build may also read auth and Stripe environment variables, but their names are not visible in the files shown, so I only set DATABASE_URL.
The build failed with 'Neither apiKey nor config.authenticator provided' because the Stripe client is created at module load in the webhook route and needs an API key during page data collection. A placeholder Stripe key addresses that. The Prisma client also needs generating because install scripts were off. The other env vars are placeholders for auth, the webhook secret, and the Gemini key that the code likely reads at load time. The exact variable names are inferred from the Stripe, Auth.js and Google AI conventions since the source was not shown.

review.summary: Bumping stripe-node from 17.3.0 to 23.0.0 and pinning both clients to "2026-09-30.endive" is the core of this change, and it looks consistent. Because stripe-node types `apiVersion` as a literal, a passing typecheck suggests the string matches the pinned SDK version. I could not independently confirm the version name; check the SDK's `apiVersion` type or the CHANGELOG. The removed `constructEventWithoutVerification` was never used: the webhook calls `webhooks.constructEvent`. The diff also adds a change the cited API change does not force: it drops `payment_method_types: ["card"]` from Checkout. The only new check is a script the agent wrote, which greps for the agent's own edits. Nothing exercises a live Stripe call or a webhook payload under the new API version. A 6-major-version and ~2-year API-version jump marked `verified` overstates what typecheck and build prove; `needs-review` fits better.

concerns.issue: Line ~136 removes `payment_method_types: ["card"]` from `checkout.sessions.create`. The cited changelog entry does not require this. Without it, Checkout falls back to dynamic payment methods configured in the Stripe Dashboard. Subscription customers may then see wallets, Link, bank debits and so on instead of card only, which changes checkout behaviour and possibly which payment methods are offered. If endive deprecates the parameter, the PR should cite that. Otherwise it should be a deliberate product decision, not a side effect of the migration.

The `stripe-migration` check is the agent's own grep script. It asserts that `payment_method_types` is absent, that the version string is present, and that node_modules has stripe 23.x. It is tautological: it proves the edit was made, not that the edit is correct. It also writes migration-specific scaffolding into the repo and reads node_modules directly. It should probably not be merged, and it should not count as evidence for a `verified` grade.

The handler reads `session.invoice`, `session.subscription`, `session.customer`, `session.amount_total` and `session.status` from `checkout.session.completed`. Webhook payload shape follows the API version configured on the webhook endpoint in the Dashboard, not the SDK's `apiVersion`. The types now describe endive while the endpoint may still send acacia-shaped events, or the reverse. Typecheck cannot catch that mismatch, and no test sends a real or fixture event.

Moving from 2024-09-30.acacia to 2026-09-30.endive crosses several breaking API releases. These include basil's billing and subscription changes, for example `current_period_*` moving to subscription items, plus whatever later versions changed. Current code only reads `sub.status`, `subsData.status`, `checkoutSession.url` and `portal.url`, so it likely survives. Still, `subscriptions.list`, `subscriptions.retrieve` and `billingPortal.sessions.create` were never exercised against the live API.

stripe 23 declares `engines.node >=20`, versus `>=12` before. The deploy runtime (Vercel or another Node host) must run Node 20 or later. The `qs` and `@types/node` dependencies were dropped, and `@types/node` is now a peer dependency; the existing `^20` devDependency satisfies it.

This one is pre-existing, not introduced by the diff. The catch block returns 200 with "Something went wrong", and non-completed events return undefined. Signature or parsing failures after the upgrade would therefore be silent and Stripe would not retry. That makes a post-upgrade webhook regression hard to notice.

checkFirst: Was removing `payment_method_types: ["card"]` intended, and what payment methods are enabled in the Dashboard for this account? If the removal was not intended, restore the parameter.
Check the API version on the webhook endpoint in the Stripe Dashboard, then send a test `checkout.session.completed` event via the Stripe CLI to confirm the Prisma insert still works.
Run one test-mode checkout end to end on endive: create the session, complete it, trigger the webhook, then call `checkSubscriptionStatus` and `createCustomerPortal`.
Confirm the deploy runtime is Node 20 or later.
Decide whether `scripts/check-stripe-migration.js` should be dropped from the PR, and whether the grade should be `needs-review` rather than `verified`.
